legacy_defects: a cancel of an import job record left active by a stopped engine (no worker owns the destination lease) is accepted: the record turns cancelling and a <id>.cancel marker is written that no worker will consume; the next status read marks the record interrupted and the marker stays (docket cancelling-an-orphaned-desktop-import-job-leaves)
scope: Legacy boundary of the desktop V1-import routes (P01 F9) on a disposable V2 data root and synthetic V1 sources inside one temp root, through the real desktop app (engine/launch.py load_app, its TokenGate and the real recovery hook). Every process launch is refused and recorded (none happens); supervisor.send_message, the recovery's admission of an imported agent's turn, is a recorder that accepts or holds as each case sets; the process's boot build identity is seeded the way an installed runtime reads it, so the replay does not run git against a source checkout; the destination Claude profile resolves inside the temp root (USERPROFILE). Legacy conformance evidence only: not a runtime census, not PostgreSQL or Rust qualification.
